name: Batch 21 · Four songs with character
status: Published to separate Spotify audition and atomically appended to hosted Playlist Lab. Four exact unrated candidates, prior feedback/history preservation and unchanged main Spotify orders verified.

selection_policy.authorization: Host October 30 explicitly corrected the modeling detour and requested a small convincing Grove test, fewer than 15 allowed. No predictive model or quantitative publication gate.
selection_policy.method: Human-style editorial selection from all 127 canonical Keeps and 846 Cuts; candidate-specific positive and negative comparisons; independent full-text lyric checks; four distinct lead artists; no quota filling.
selection_policy.brief: Upbeat, interesting, bouncy, melodic, sexy, fun, happy, hopeful and loving; personality, strong hooks and development. Avoid blandness, low perceived energy, dragging repetition, standalone intros/interludes/outros and artist/album overrepresentation. No acid/techno; avoid chart-pop/top-five-hit character and sad/negative lyrics. Existing individual Keeps remain approved.
selection_policy.evidence_limit: Musical fit remains editorial inference. Attempted preview-audio input was explicitly unsupported; no direct listening or full-arrangement proof claimed. Full published song text reviewed; no full lyrics exported.

feedback_basis.policy: canonical feedback with host priority; all individual histories preserved

tracks.title: Hey Cowboy
tracks.selection_hypothesis: A teasing sung invitation with country-flavoured phrasing and a verse/chorus/bridge scene, rather than using a confidence slogan as the entire hook. Compare the wry vocal persona in W.I.T.C.H. and the explicit attraction in yes baby.
tracks.cut_warning: Those Cuts show that sexual confidence and a catchy refrain alone are insufficient. Test whether this particular vocal phrasing, smile and changing sections have appeal; the country tint is a real taste risk.

mood_screen.status: published full song text reviewed; no exact-master transcription claim
mood_screen.summary: Flirtatious, sexually self-directed casual encounter. The bridge explicitly makes it a one-night good time; not a romantic commitment, breakup or insult narrative.

tracks.title: Lone Digger
tracks.keep_comparison: A Night Like This; Would You...?; Makeba - Radio Edit
tracks.selection_hypothesis: The proposed case is an angular brass/reed figure interacting with the bass and a fully sung dance invitation: a test of physical bounce plus an identifiable instrumental hook, alongside the sensual/playful Caro Emerald and Touch & Go Keeps.
tracks.cut_warning: Retro or jazzy styling gets no exemption: the earlier broad retro pass failed. Shake Your Coconuts also shows that a playful dance command is insufficient. Test this exact riff/vocal combination rather than opening another electro-swing lane.

mood_screen.status: published full song text reviewed; no exact-master transcription claim
mood_screen.summary: Sung encouragement to dance, move together and enjoy the party. No heartbreak narrative in the reviewed text; occasional forceful dance-command wording.

tracks.title: Let's Go
tracks.keep_comparison: Daylight; Heart It Races; Float On
tracks.selection_hypothesis: A wordless melodic refrain, sung verses and a contrasting verbal bridge provide more than the title chant. Investigate the drum/keyboard lift and communal release already represented by Daylight, without requiring a house arrangement.
tracks.cut_warning: The rejected upbeat indie anthems prevent calling optimism or a big chorus sufficient. The test is the particular melodic refrain and release from self-consciousness, not a general indie-pop expansion.

mood_screen.status: published full song text reviewed; no exact-master transcription claim
mood_screen.summary: Leaving overthinking behind, singing freely and making words count. Brief opening self-consciousness is resolved; the central framing is release rather than sadness or relationship loss.

tracks.title: The Golden Age
tracks.keep_comparison: A Night Like This; The Walker; Mushaboom
tracks.selection_hypothesis: A bright horn-led song with an eccentric lead voice, an aspirational narrative and a separate sung refrain. The proposed connection is theatrical personality plus forward-moving melody, not retro texture alone.
tracks.cut_warning: Fascination and Safe and Sound are direct warnings against equating brass, brightness or a radio-sized chorus with a Keep. Test the distinctive vocal character and theatrical verses; broad happy-indie sourcing is not reopened.

mood_screen.status: published full song text reviewed; no exact-master transcription claim
mood_screen.summary: Playful fantasy of performing, dressing up, making it and feeling free; nostalgic but affirmative. Alcohol/tobacco/casino imagery, without a central loss or breakup narrative.
